title: K08 human caption reconstruction rank fixed before commitment tests
ranking_criterion: Ranks 1-10 directly express N13 late-night domestic image and N20 sea/table inclusivity with ordinary syntax; 11-20 explore a softer poetic voice; 21-30 are more figurative or depict a specific watch moment. Source mail/11 rules out a formal technical title and N17/N18 identify unrelated labels. All are hypothetical new sentences.

phrases.caption: There is always room for another cup when the sea turns pale outside the window.
At the end of the night, the sea was quiet and there was still room at the table.
The lamp stays on and the sea waits outside until everyone has found a place at the table.
By the time the sea grows light, there is still room for one more cup.
The sea outside the window can wait until everyone has had their tea.
At the end of the watch, we leave a light and a place for whoever comes next.
The mugs are by the window and the sea is almost morning.
There is room at the table until the last voice has gone quiet.
When the sea is dark and the watch runs late, there is always room for another voice.
The last light of the night belongs to anyone who needs a place to sit.
Somewhere between the last cup and the first light, we make room for each other.
When the night is nearly over, the sea can wait while we pour one more cup.
The sea beyond the window, the lamp on, and one more chair pulled up to the table.
At the end of a long night there is still a little light and a place at the table.
The morning comes over the sea and the table still has room for one more.
We always leave a light on and a cup ready for the next watch.
The sea looks kinder with a warm cup and someone waiting at the table.
The night ends with the sea outside and everyone making room at the table.
Before the first boat comes, there is time for one more cup by the window.
The last cup is never the last if someone else is still awake.
The little lamp stays on while the sea turns from night to morning.
At the window the sea is changing colour, and nobody has to finish their tea alone.
The room is ready for morning when there is a chair for everyone still awake.
The sea outside and the quiet voices around the table mean the night is almost over.
By the window the mugs wait for another voice at the end of the night.
The last hour of the watch belongs to tea, the sea, and the people who stay.
When the sea comes back into view, everyone still has a place at the table.
The night is nearly done, the sea is still outside, and the kettle is on.
Nobody finishes the last cup alone when the night watch comes in.
The sea beyond the window is quiet enough to hear everyone at the table.
